answer.summary: Lord says frontier-model builders need high-quality data first, plus large volumes and fast turnaround, because poor data is hard to overcome and researchers rapidly test and expand whichever data pipelines improve a model. Providers should also assess data’s impact and work closely with researchers.

sections.heading: What builders need—and why
sections.content: Lord names three priorities: quality, volume, and speed. Quality comes first: like teaching a student, giving a model the wrong data is extremely challenging to overcome. Builders also need thousands of high-quality examples in advanced areas such as chemistry, mathematics, and physics. Speed matters because teams test several hypotheses or pipelines; when one shows a gain, they quickly expand it and may drop two or three efforts that do not improve the model.

sections.heading: What providers should deliver
sections.content: Providers need to turn around data in days and then scale the high-quality data that is helping. Lord describes using top-GPA students from Stanford, Berkeley, and MIT to generate physics data. His company assesses each unit of data to estimate whether it improves a capability, and brings its own research and post-training teams and GPUs to work directly with researchers—sharing what it observes about the data and how it could improve the model or be used in training.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately covers Lord’s three priorities: high-quality data because incorrect data is difficult for models to overcome, large volumes in advanced domains, and fast turnaround so researchers can test hypotheses and scale pipelines that show gains. Its additional details about assessing data and working with researchers are supported by the cited context.
